reason: REFUTED ON THE LOCATOR, not on the words. The wording is sound and I could not break it: Open Library's search inside returns the full string you have never done enough, so long as it is still possible that you have something of value to contribute from scans of Markings itself, including the edition catalogued under Leif Sjoberg and W. H. Auden, and returns the continuation of value to contribute. This is the answer when you are groaning under what you... from the body of several Markings scans. So the sentence is Hammarskjold's, it is in the Sjoberg and Auden text, and the shorter anthology wording the verifier's note rejects is indeed the corrupt one. The translator credit and the 1964 Knopf date are right. The defect is that the verifier, unable to confirm the page it started with, DROPPED the locator altogether and left the source line as Dag Hammarskjold, Markings (trans. Leif Sjoberg and W. H. Auden, 1964). That names a two-hundred-page book of several hundred unnumbered aphorisms and nothing else. Rule 4 is explicit that every candidate carries a LOCATABLE citation: work, AND book, chapter, letter, section or line, or else edition and page. A bare title is not a locator, and a reader who wanted to check this line could not find it. The verifier's own note compounds the error by calling it an undated entry. Markings is not undated: I confirmed against Wikiquote's Dag Hammarskjold page that the book is organised throughout under year headings, from 1925-1930 to Whitsunday 1961, and every entry sits under one. So there IS a locator to be had, the year heading, and nobody has gone and got it. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: establish the year heading the passage falls under, or a page in a named printing, and put it in the source line. I tried and failed to get either. Archive.org's scans of Markings are lending-restricted, so the djvu text returns 403 and the BookReader search endpoint 404; the Google Books API returned 429; search inside gives the string but no page; Wikiquote does not carry this passage at all. WebSearch was unavailable, the session budget being spent, so I could not chase the secondary citations that would give a page. I therefore offer no betterCitation rather than mint a plausible page, which is the failure this track exists to prevent. A confident false page is worse than an honest gap. SECONDARY NOTE for whoever picks this up: the line reads as a hard saying at six in the morning (you have never done enough), and the sentence that follows it in the book, This is the answer when you are groaning under what you consider a burden, is the consolation that turns it. If it comes back with a locator, consider whether it wants that second sentence with it. Everything else passes: shipped.js gives dag hammarskjold at 1 of 3 from month 7, not banned, not shipped, no near opening; Markings is a real posthumously published journal so the Diary tag is the form of the work; in scope at 1963 and 1964; publishable; the source leads with the name, has no dash and runs 70 characters.
